title: Worksheet 14: Type Conversion (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Type conversion, sometimes called "type casting," is the process of changing a value from one data type into another, such as converting a string into an integer or converting an integer into a float. Type conversion is often necessary because different data types behave differently, and a program may need a value in a specific type before it can be used correctly; for example, a number typed into a text input box by a user is often initially stored as a string, even if it looks like a number, and must be converted into an integer or float before any math can be performed on it. Some type conversions are straightforward, such as converting the string "5" into the integer 5, but others can fail or cause errors, such as attempting to convert the string "hello" into an integer, since there is no numeric value that "hello" could reasonably represent. Programmers often need to check or handle these potential errors carefully, especially when converting data that came from outside the program, such as information typed in by a user, since that data cannot always be trusted to be in the expected format.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, type conversion is the process of:
questions.correct: Changing a value from one data type into another
distractors: Deleting a value the program no longer needs
Giving a variable a new name
Sorting values from smallest to largest
